summary: A widow or divorced woman says she married as a maiden, and her husband says she was a widow. If witnesses saw her wedding done the way maidens' weddings were done, she gets two hundred.

chunks.en: A woman who became a widow or was divorced,

chunks.en: and he says,
chunks.st: and he says:

chunks.en: No, I married you as a widow.
chunks.st: No; rather, I married you as a widow, who is entitled to one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: If there are witnesses that she went out to her wedding
chunks.st: then, if there are witnesses that she went out of her father’s house to her wedding

summary: If someone says, This field was your father's and I bought it from him, he is believed, because the same mouth that made the problem also took it away. But if there are witnesses it was the father's, he is not believed.
stIntro: Several disputes between Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua were cited previously with regard to the credibility accorded to the respective claims of parties to a dispute. Based on one of those disputes, the tanna adds:

chunks.he: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵרוֹ שָׂדֶה
chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua agrees about a man who tells his friend, This field
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehoshua concedes in a case where one says to another: This field, which is currently in my possession,

chunks.he: זוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיךָ הָיְתָה וּלְקַחְתִּיהָ הֵימֶנּוּ,
chunks.en: was your father's, and I bought it from him,
chunks.st: belonged to your father and I purchased it from him,

chunks.en: that he is believed,
chunks.st: that he is deemed credible,
chunks.stMore: and his entire claim is accepted. The court accepts not only his admission that it once belonged to the other’s father, but also his statement that he purchased it.

chunks.en: because the mouth that made it forbidden is the mouth that made it allowed.
chunks.explain: Without his words, we would not know it was the father's.
chunks.st: This is so, as the mouth that prohibited, i.e., claimed that the field had belonged to the other’s father, is the mouth that permitted,
chunks.stMore: i.e., claimed that he purchased the field. Even if he had not admitted that it had belonged to the other’s father, the field would have remained in his possession. Therefore, his claim is accepted.

chunks.en: But if there are witnesses that it belonged
chunks.st: However, if there are witnesses that the field belonged to

chunks.en: to his father, and he says, I bought it from him,
chunks.st: his father, and the one who has the field in his possession says: I purchased it from him,

chunks.en: he is not believed.
chunks.st: he is not deemed credible and his claim is rejected.

summary: Witnesses who say, This is our signature, but we were forced, or too young, or not kosher witnesses, are believed. But if their signatures can be proven without them, they are not believed.

chunks.he: הָעֵדִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ כְּתַב יָדֵינוּ הוּא זֶה,
chunks.en: Witnesses who said, This is our handwriting,
chunks.st: the witnesses who said in their testimony to ratify their signatures in a document: We signed the document and this is our handwriting;

chunks.en: but we were forced to sign,
chunks.st: however, we were compelled to sign, or

chunks.en: we were children,
chunks.st: we were minors when we signed, or

chunks.en: we were not allowed to be witnesses,
chunks.st: we were disqualified witnesses, e.g., we are relatives of one of the parties,

chunks.en: they are believed.
chunks.st: they are deemed credible.
chunks.stMore: Since the document is ratified on the basis of their testimony, it is likewise invalidated on the basis of their testimony.

chunks.en: But if there are other witnesses that it is their
chunks.st: However, if there are other witnesses who testify

chunks.en: handwriting, or their handwriting
chunks.st: that it is their handwriting, or if their handwriting

chunks.en: shows up on a paper from another place,
chunks.st: emerges on a document from another place,
chunks.stMore: enabling confirmation of their signatures by comparing the two documents,

chunks.en: they are not believed.
chunks.st: then the witnesses who signed the document are not deemed credible.
chunks.stMore: The document is not invalidated based on their testimony, because ratification of the document is not dependent on their testimony, as their signatures can be authenticated independently.

summary: Two witnesses can prove that their signatures on a document are real. Rebbi says each one must also be backed up by another person; the Sages say each man is believed about his own signature.

chunks.en: One says, This is my handwriting,
chunks.st: this witness whose name is signed on a document says: This is my handwriting

chunks.en: and this is my friend's handwriting,
chunks.st: and this is the handwriting of my fellow witness,

chunks.en: and the other says, This is my handwriting,
chunks.st: and that witness says: This is my handwriting

chunks.en: and this is my friend's handwriting,
chunks.st: and that is the handwriting of my fellow witness,

chunks.en: they are believed.
chunks.st: these witnesses are deemed credible
chunks.stMore: and the document is ratified, as together they provide testimony authenticating both signatures.

chunks.en: If one says, This is my handwriting,
chunks.st: If this witness says: This is my handwriting,

chunks.en: and the other says, This is my handwriting,
chunks.st: and that witness says: This is my handwriting,
chunks.stMore: and neither testifies with regard to the signature of the other,

chunks.en: they need another person to join them.
chunks.st: they must add another witness with them
chunks.stMore: who will authenticate the signatures of the two witnesses, as otherwise, each of the witnesses would be testifying with regard to half the sum in the document;

chunks.en: That is what Rebbi says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who wrote down the Mishnah.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: they do not need another person to join them.
chunks.st: They need not add another witness with them.

chunks.en: Rather, a person is believed to say,
chunks.st: Rather, a person is deemed credible to say:

chunks.en: This is my handwriting.
chunks.st: This is my handwriting.
chunks.stMore: The testimony of the two signatories about their own signatures is sufficient.

summary: A woman who says, I was married and now I am divorced, is believed, because without her words we would not know she was married. The same is true for a woman who says she was taken captive but stayed pure.

chunks.en: she is believed, because the mouth that made it forbidden is the mouth that made it allowed.

chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: But where nobody argues,

summary: A woman held by goyim may sometimes not stay married to her Kohen husband, because we worry something bad was done to her. Witnesses can help her, but a husband cannot speak up for his own wife.

chunks.en: A woman who was locked up by goyim
chunks.st: a woman who was imprisoned by gentiles

chunks.en: because of money (a debt),
chunks.st: due to a monetary
chunks.stMore: offense committed by her husband, once she is released after he pays his debt,

chunks.en: may stay with her husband.
chunks.st: she is permitted to her husband,
chunks.stMore: even if he is a priest. There is no concern that they violated her because their objective is to coerce the husband to pay his debt in exchange for her release. Were they to abuse her, it is possible that he would be unwilling to pay.

chunks.en: If it was because of a crime punished by death,
chunks.st: However, if a woman was imprisoned due to a capital

chunks.st: And a person is not deemed credible to establish his status by his own

summary: Grown-ups are believed about some things they saw when they were children, like whose handwriting this is, or that someone was a Kohen. But they are not believed when it would take land away from someone.
